name: Harrenhal
description: Greatest and unluckiest castle in Westeros, its towers melted by dragonfire three centuries ago. Arya served Tywin here as cupbearer; Jaime lost a hand nearby, confessed in its baths and leapt into its bear pit for Brienne.

name: Riverrun
description: Moated seat of House Tully at the joining of two rivers. Robb was proclaimed King in the North here; years later Jaime ended the Blackfish's last stand by turning Edmure against his own walls.

name: The Twins
description: Twin castles bridging the Green Fork, toll-gate of the north and seat of Walder Frey. The Red Wedding drowned its hall in Stark blood — and Arya Stark returned twice to collect the debt.

name: Crossroads Inn
description: The famous inn where the kingsroad meets the river road. Catelyn seized Tyrion here; Arya reclaimed Needle from Polliver here; and Hot Pie bakes here still, twice pointing Brienne and Arya on their way.

name: Stoney Sept
description: Largest town of the riverlands, remembered for the Battle of the Bells in Robert's Rebellion. Book background in the show's era.

name: High Heart
description: Sacred hill ringed by weirwood stumps, haunted by old gods' dreams. The Brotherhood's ghost-seeress dwells here in the books; the show keeps only its wild riverland setting.

name: Hollow Hill
description: Hidden cave-hall of the Brotherhood Without Banners, where the Hound was tried by fire against Beric Dondarrion and Arya watched a dead man rise again.

name: Stone Mill
description: Mill on the Red Fork where Edmure Tully threw back the Mountain's raiders — a 'victory' that wrecked Robb's trap and cost the Stark cause dearly.

name: Darry
description: Castle of House Darry near the kingsroad. The confrontation over Arya's direwolf happened in its lands in Season 1. Otherwise book background.

name: Maidenpool
description: Port town on the Bay of Crabs where Florian first saw Jonquil bathing, or so the songs say. Book background in the show.

name: Seagard
description: Fortified port of House Mallister, raised to guard against ironborn raids. Book background only.

name: Stone Hedge
description: Seat of House Bracken on the Red Fork, ancient rivals of the Blackwoods across the river. Book background only.

name: Raventree Hall
description: Seat of House Blackwood beneath a dead weirwood full of ravens. Book background only.

name: Acorn Hall
description: Keep of House Smallwood in the riverland woods, a stop on Arya's book travels with the Brotherhood. Background in the show.

name: Pinkmaiden
description: Castle of House Piper on the Red Fork. Book background only.

name: Antlers
description: Castle of House Buckwell northeast of King's Landing. Book background only.

name: Sow's Horn
description: Holdfast of House Hogg near the crownland border. Book background only.

name: Brindlewood
description: Village on the kingsroad approach to King's Landing. Book background only.

name: Ivy Inn
description: Roadside inn on the kingsroad south of the Trident. Book background only.

name: Trident Village
description: One of the countless riverland villages burned and re-burned as armies crossed the Trident — the war's quiet casualties.

name: Riverlands Holdfast
description: Fortified refuge typical of the riverland smallfolk, offering thin protection from the War of the Five Kings.

name: Rushing Falls
description: Falls of the upper Blackwater Rush. Book background geography.

name: Tumbler's Falls
description: River town at the falls of the Blackwater Rush. Book background only.

name: Riverland Sept
description: Country sept of the riverlands — kin to the quiet septry where the Hound found brief peace with Brother Ray's flock before the Brotherhood's renegades came.

name: Mummer's Ford
description: Ford on the Red Fork where, in the books, Beric Dondarrion's party was ambushed by the Mountain — the errand Ned sent him on in Season 1.

name: Sherrer
description: Village put to the sword in the Mountain's raids — its survivors petitioned Ned Stark on the Iron Throne in Season 1.

name: Wendish Town
description: Riverland town burned in Gregor Clegane's raids, named among the ruins reported to the Iron Throne.

name: Lord Goodbrook's Village
description: Village of a minor riverland house. Book background only.

name: Sallydance
description: Riverland village of the books, plundered in the war. Book background only.

name: Lady of the Leaves' Village
description: Hidden treetop village of war refugees from the books. Book background only.

name: Lord Lychester's Keep
description: Small keep of a broken riverland house. Book background only.

name: Trident Hamlet
description: Nameless hamlet of the war-torn Trident country. Book background only.

name: Inn of the Lion Banner
description: Roadside inn that hosted Lannister soldiery in the war years — the kind of place Arya and the Hound learned to eat at quietly.

name: Inn of the Kneeling Man
description: Trident inn named for the king who knelt to Aegon the Conqueror. In the books, Arya's party is taken by the Brotherhood here.

name: Brotherhood Hideout
description: One of the Brotherhood Without Banners' scattered boltholes in the riverland hills — the outlaws who fight for the smallfolk of no king.

name: Lord Harroway's Town
description: Trident crossing town of the books, half-drowned by the wars' seasons. Book background only.

name: Quiet Isle
description: Monastic island at the mouth of the Trident where broken men heal in silence. The show's Brother Ray sept storyline borrows its spirit.

name: Fairmarket
description: Market town on the Blue Fork. Book background only.

name: Oldstones
description: Ruined hilltop castle of the ancient river kings, where in the books Robb holds council. Background in the show.

name: Palisade Village
description: Stockaded village of the northern riverlands. Book background only.

name: Pennytree
description: Village around an ancient oak studded with pennies for luck. Book background only.
